name: LLVM GlobalISel
listed_description: LLVM's modular, whole-function instruction selection framework built from standalone Machine IR passes (IRTranslator, Legalizer, InstructionSelect); intended as the balanced successor to SelectionDAG and as a candidate for fast compile at O0.
claim_text: Book cites a 2019 Apple LLVM Dev talk: GlobalISel matched SDISel quality on their GPU backend at about two times the speed; a 2017 report put it 1.1 to 1.2 times slower than FastISel on AArch64.
book_benchmark: Second-hand figures only: compile time of GlobalISel versus SelectionDAG (Apple GPU backend, 2019 talk) and versus FastISel (AArch64, 2017). Book gives no compiler flags, workload or CPU and ran nothing itself.
guessed_baseline: LLVM SelectionDAG instruction selector (SDISel); FastISel for O0
found_in: book: LLVM Code Generation (2025), ch. 14, section Compile time (comparison of instruction selectors)

name: LLVM FastISel
listed_description: LLVM's one-pass sub-selector inside SelectionDAG that goes straight from LLVM IR to Machine IR, built for the fastest compile time at the cost of generality; falls back to SelectionDAG for unsupported IR.
claim_text: Compile time of FastISel is usually faster than the other two frameworks; when all IR goes through it, compile time is described as blazing fast. SDISel can take about 20% of total backend compile time.
book_benchmark: No measurement in the book; qualitative claim plus a rule-of-thumb share (SDISel about 20% of backend compile time, backend includes IR optimization passes). No flags, CPU or workload stated.
found_in: book: LLVM Code Generation (2025), ch. 14, sections Overview of the selectors and Compile time

name: LLVM register units for physical register overlap checks
listed_description: TableGen-computed minimal set of leaf units that captures every register and alias, so availability and interference checks touch fewer entities than walking the full register hierarchy (MCRegUnit, LiveRegUnits).
claim_text: Register units are a compile-time life-saving mechanism; in the toy hierarchy, checking q0 needs three unit checks instead of five alias checks.
book_benchmark: Toy example only (9 registers mapped onto 5 units, 3 versus 5 checks). No timings, compiler or hardware.
guessed_baseline: enumerating the full register alias hierarchy
found_in: book: LLVM Code Generation (2025), ch. 11, section The concept of register units
